text:
# SEO and GEO audit: quay-store (SvelteKit)

Findings are ordered by severity. I read all 9 tracked files. I didn't build or run the app, so these come from reading the source.

## Critical

**1. Googlebot is blocked from the whole site.** `static/robots.txt:4-5`
`User-agent: Googlebot` followed by `Disallow: /` blocks Google Search entirely. Googlebot obeys only its own, more specific group, so the `Allow: /` in the `*` group doesn't apply to it.
Fix: delete lines 4-5. If you want to block specific paths, list them under `User-agent: *`.

**2. No server-side rendering.** `src/routes/+layout.ts:1`
`export const ssr = false;` makes every page an empty shell in the initial HTML.
- Most AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and similar) don't run JavaScript. They see no content, no `<title>`, no meta tags and no JSON-LD.
- Googlebot has to render the page first, which delays indexing and can lose content.

Fix: remove the line, or set `ssr = true`. If you need SPA behaviour, turn it off only on specific routes that really need it, and add `export const prerender = true;` for static pages.

## High

**3. Empty meta description on the shop page.** `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:3`
`content=""` gives search engines and AI summarisers nothing to use as a snippet.
Fix: write a real description, for example "Bilge pumps, cleats and rope for boats. Shipped next day."

**4. Product schema is invalid and thin.** `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:5`
- `Product` has only a `name`. Google's rich results need an `offers` block (price, `priceCurrency`, `availability`) or a review or rating. Add `image` and `description` too.
- This is a category page listing several items, so a single `Product` is the wrong type. Use `CollectionPage` with an `ItemList`, or give each real product its own `Product` markup.
- The `{@html ...}` template works, but a `</script>` in any dynamic value would break out of the tag. If you add data later, escape `<` in the JSON (`JSON.stringify(...).replace(/</g, '\\u003c')`).

**5. Homepage has no structured data.** `src/routes/+page.svelte:1-5`
Add `Organization` and `WebSite` JSON-LD with name, URL, logo and `sameAs` links. This is the main signal AI engines use to identify the brand as an entity.

## Medium

**6. `<html>` has no `lang` attribute.** `src/app.html:2`
Fix: `<html lang="en-GB">`. The £ in the layout suggests UK English.

**7. No viewport meta tag.** `src/app.html:4`
Without `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />`, mobile rendering suffers, and Google indexes mobile-first.

**8. `data-nosnippet` hides the delivery info.** `src/routes/+layout.svelte:7`
`data-nosnippet` stops "Free delivery over £50." from appearing in Google snippets and AI Overviews. That is useful commercial information for shoppers. Remove the attribute unless you want it hidden. Also, the text sits outside any landmark; wrap it in `<footer>` or `<aside>`.

**9. Weak and inconsistent titles.**
- `src/routes/search/+page.svelte:2`: "Search" has no brand name. Use "Search | Quay".
- `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:2`: "Shop all parts" has no brand and no keywords. Use something like "Boat Parts: Bilge Pumps, Cleats & Rope | Quay".
- `src/routes/+page.svelte:2`: "Quay: boat parts" is fine, but make the separator match the others.

**10. Thin content.** `src/routes/+page.svelte:7` and `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:8-9`
Each page is one heading plus one line. Pages like this rank poorly and give AI engines nothing to cite. Add product listings with names, prices and descriptions, links to product pages, and an FAQ or shipping and returns section with concrete facts (delivery times, cut-off, returns window).

## Low

**11. Sitemap is missing `<lastmod>`.** `static/sitemap.xml:3-4`
Add accurate `lastmod` dates. Better, generate the file from your routes and product data so it doesn't go stale. `/search` is correctly left out because it's `noindex`.

**12. Search page: `noindex` with no `follow` hint, and no description.** `src/routes/search/+page.svelte:3`
This is acceptable as is. Consider `noindex, follow` so the links on it are still crawled.

**13. No social or Open Graph tags anywhere.** All pages
Add `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`, `og:url`, `og:type` and `twitter:card`. Put the shared defaults in the layout and override them per page.

**14. Canonical URLs are hardcoded and on the placeholder domain.** `src/routes/+page.svelte:4`, `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:4`, `static/robots.txt:7`, `static/sitemap.xml`
All of these use `quay.example`. Make sure the real domain replaces it before launch, ideally from one shared config value. The search page has no canonical, which is fine given `noindex`.

**15. Navigation and landmarks.** `src/routes/+layout.svelte:5`, `src/app.html:8`
Add `aria-label="Main"` to the `<nav>`. Use `<main>` around the page content, and drop the extra `<div>` wrapper in `app.html`.

## GEO-specific gaps (no file yet)

- **No `llms.txt`.** Optional, and its benefit is unproven, but cheap to add at `static/llms.txt` with a site summary and key links.
- **No AI-crawler policy.** `robots.txt` doesn't name GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and similar. Once finding 1 is fixed, decide whether to allow them explicitly.
- **No author, brand or about page.** AI engines favour sources with clear entity information. Add an About or Contact page with address, company details and policies.

## Suggested fix order
1. Remove the Googlebot block (#1).
2. Re-enable SSR (#2).
3. Fix `lang`, viewport and the empty description (#6, #7, #3).
4. Correct the structured data and add Organization markup (#4, #5).
5. Add real content to the pages (#10).

I haven't changed anything. I can apply the quick fixes (#1, #2, #3, #6, #7, #8, #9) if you want.
